name: Ashiana Housing
tagline: Debt-light senior-living developer riding a genuine demographic tailwind (~Rs8,000cr GDV pipeline), but 32.5x trailing P/E and a historically weak ROCE track record (just inflecting) cap conviction at Medium
verdict_headline: Genuine senior-living demographic tailwind and disciplined, internally-funded growth, but a historically weak ROCE track record (just inflecting) and an already-full ~32.5x multiple keep conviction at Medium rather than higher
verdict_reasoning: Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes; moat weak, valuation weak) permits the 10x-in-2-3-years label -- senior-living GDV pipeline (~Rs8,000cr of ~Rs16,000cr total) against a ~26% CAGR, structurally underpenetrated Indian senior-living TAM (Mordor Intelligence) is a real, primary-source-adjacent headroom case

Demand signal confirmed beyond investor-deck narrative: FY26 bookings ~+25% YoY to a record, collections +40% YoY to Rs1,484cr, FY27 presales guidance Rs2,200cr already tracking (YTD Rs859cr by late Jul-2026, H1 exit guided Rs1,050-1,100cr)

Capital discipline is real: D/E 0.30, Debt/CFO ~0.5x (ICRA), both ICRA (Sep-2025) and CARE (Dec-2025) reaffirmed stable ratings, zero promoter pledge, and new senior-living land (Pune, Chennai, Maharashtra) acquired largely off internal accruals rather than fresh debt

Held back from a higher conviction: 3-yr average ROCE (FY23-25) was just 6.2% (median 3.7%, screener.in) and even FY26's inflection to 14.0% falls just short of the 15% Coffee-Can hurdle; moat is weak (premium pricing/lifestyle differentiation, but no structural barrier against PE-backed entrants like Antara/Columbia Pacific); valuation is already full at ~32.5x trailing P/E / ~4.4x P/B

No red flag: no pledge, no auditor resignation or SEBI action found, ratings stable-to-improving; RPT trend and a clean net-debt/EBITDA figure could not be cleanly sourced this pass -- flagged as open questions, not treated as negative
business_overview: Ashiana Housing is a 45+ year-old pan-India residential developer (8 cities) now pivoting toward senior living as its primary growth engine -- the segment was ~41% of Q1 FY27 bookings (up from ~25%+ a year earlier) against a stated medium-term target of ~50%, alongside kid-centric and premium/elite residential formats. The company is debt-light (D/E 0.30, Debt/CFO ~0.5x per ICRA) and funds its ~Rs425cr/year senior-living capex largely from internal collections. FY27 presales guidance is Rs2,200cr, building on FY26's record bookings (~+25% YoY) and FY25's then-record Rs1,937cr.
fundamentals_table: Rs 1,143 Cr (+116% YoY, record; completion-method, lumpy)
~Rs 2,400 Cr est. (~+25% YoY, record); FY27 guidance Rs 2,200 Cr
ICRA reaffirmed (Sep-2025); CARE A; Stable reaffirmed (Dec-2025, Rs454.08cr NCDs)
fundamentals_narrative: Revenue recognition follows the completion method, so P&L revenue is lumpy and a poor quarter-to-quarter read (Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs107cr from Rs293cr YoY even as bookings and collections grew) -- bookings/presales and collections are the cleaner demand signals, and both have grown every year since FY24. ROCE has historically been weak (FY23-25 3-yr average just 6.2%, median 3.7% per screener.in) and FY26's 14.0% print, while a real inflection, still falls just short of the Coffee-Can 15% hurdle. At ~32.5x trailing P/E and ~4.4x P/B, the market is already paying up for the senior-living growth story; both ICRA (Sep-2025) and CARE (Dec-2025) reaffirmed stable ratings, and promoter holding (61.11%) has been flat with zero pledge throughout.
bull_case: Structural, underpenetrated senior-living TAM (India market ~USD3.55bn in 2025 -> ~USD14.14bn by 2031, ~26% CAGR, Mordor Intelligence) with Ashiana an early, premium-positioned mover (Rs15,200/sqft realizations vs Rs7,000-10,000/sqft industry floor)
Demand is real and growing across every available data point: bookings ~+25% YoY (FY26, record), collections +40% YoY to Rs1,484cr, Q1 FY27 presales tracking toward FY27's Rs2,200cr guidance

Debt-light, internally-funded growth (D/E 0.30, zero pledge, two independent rating agencies -- ICRA and CARE -- reaffirmed stable ratings through FY26/25) gives balance-sheet room to keep acquiring land (Pune 28.55 acres ~Rs1,800cr potential, Chennai MWC lease ~Rs1,200cr potential) without dilution or distress

Mix-shift up the value chain: senior living (stickier, recurring lifestyle-services revenue layered on the one-time sale, ~300 activities/month) rising from ~25% to ~41% of bookings in a year, management's stated target ~50%
FY26 ROCE inflected to 14.0% from a 6.2% 3-yr average -- the first real sign the capital-intensive build-out phase may be turning into returns
bear_case: ROCE has been weak for most of the company's recent history (FY23-25 3-yr average just 6.2%, median 3.7%) -- FY26's 14.0% is one data point, not yet a confirmed trend, and still misses the 15% Coffee-Can hurdle
At ~32.5x trailing P/E and ~4.4x P/B, the senior-living growth story is already substantially priced in -- not a cheap entry even if the demographic thesis plays out

No structural moat: Ashiana's premium pricing and lifestyle differentiation are real but not a hard barrier -- PE-backed private players (Antara, Columbia Pacific Communities, Primus) are actively expanding into the same underpenetrated niche and could compress the pricing/returns advantage over time

P&L revenue recognition (completion method) is genuinely lumpy and hard to model -- Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs107cr from Rs293cr YoY despite bookings/collections growth, and a clean trailing net-debt/EBITDA or FCF-conversion figure could not be derived cleanly this pass (source data was internally inconsistent)
Newly acquired senior-living land (Pune, Chennai, Maharashtra) is too recent to show a completed project cycle -- capex efficiency on the stepped-up ~Rs425cr/year outlay is unproven
RPT trend not assessed this pass -- an open question given promoter family concentration (61.11% combined, four individuals each >1%)

quarterly_trend: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 qtr): P&L revenue fell to Rs107.44cr from Rs292.72cr YoY on delivery/completion timing, but PAT held at Rs13.11cr (vs Rs12.72cr YoY, aided by ~Rs12.31cr other income) -- shows how disconnected quarterly P&L is from underlying demand

Q1 FY27 bookings Rs358cr (3.60 lakh sqft, 234 units) at an improved average realization of Rs9,923/sqft; collections Rs409cr and pre-tax operating cash flow Rs121cr both stayed healthy despite the revenue dip

Senior-living mix in Q1 FY27 reached 41% of the portfolio (vs 23% kid-centric, 36% elite/premium) -- up sharply from ~25%+ a year earlier, confirming the stated strategic pivot is actually showing up in the numbers, not just guidance

FY26 full-year: bookings rose ~25% YoY to a record, collections +40% YoY to Rs1,484cr, and senior-living area booked alone was Rs570.15cr (Advik, Amodh, Vatsalya, Swarang projects) -- broad-based, not one-project-dependent

FY27 guidance: Rs2,200cr full-year presales; YTD presales Rs859cr by late Jul-2026 with H1 exit guided at Rs1,050-1,100cr -- tracking plausible but requires H2 (seasonally stronger) to deliver the back-half
recent_announcements: Dec-2025: CARE Ratings reaffirmed CARE A; Stable for the issuer rating and Rs454.08cr of NCDs across five tranches
Sep-2025: ICRA reaffirmed Ashiana's rating with the rated amount enhanced, citing improved FY25 sales/collections expected to sustain into FY26
Jul/Aug-2026: Q1 FY27 results + concall -- Pune 28.55-acre senior-living land acquisition (~Rs1,800cr potential) disclosed, FY27 Rs2,200cr presales guidance reiterated
Apr-2026: FY26 results -- record annual revenue/profit/bookings announced; FY26 senior-living capex outlay of Rs425cr disclosed
key_new_facts: The 3-yr ROCE average (FY23-25) of just 6.2% (median 3.7%, screener.in) is materially weaker than the headline FY26 14.0% figure suggests on its own -- FY26 is a genuine but still-unconfirmed single-year inflection

Ashiana has no listed pure-play senior-living competitor in India; the real competitive set (Antara/Max, Columbia Pacific Communities, Primus) is private/PE-backed, which both reduces near-term competitive pressure and means there's no public comp to benchmark valuation against

Revenue recognition lumpiness is severe enough that a single quarter's P&L (Q1 FY27's Rs107cr vs Rs293cr YoY) can look like a business in decline even while bookings, collections and cash flow all improved -- bookings/collections, not quarterly P&L, are the right demand signal here

A reported FY25 operating-cash-flow figure of Rs2,335cr (vs just Rs529cr FY25 revenue) found on one aggregator is almost certainly erroneous/mismatched and was excluded from this write-up rather than used -- flagged so a future pass sources CFO directly from the annual report cash-flow statement

deep_dive.conviction_update: Low-Medium -> Medium. Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes, tam yes; moat weak, valuation weak) supports the 10x-in-2-3-years label, and primary-document-adjacent sources (ICRA/CARE rating rationales, FY26/Q1 FY27 results) confirm real demand growth (bookings ~+25% YoY, collections +40% YoY), zero pledge, and disciplined internally-funded capex. Held below Medium-High by a historically weak 3-yr ROCE average (6.2%), an already-full ~32.5x P/E, and several quality metrics that couldn't be cleanly sourced this pass.

earnings_quality.normalised_note: OPM swung roughly 6%-19% across recent quarters purely on project-completion timing, not a cyclical peak; through-cycle margin is better read off annual figures -- FY26's ~10.3% PAT margin (Rs118cr/Rs1,143cr) is a more representative base than any single quarter.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Quarterly P&L revenue is completion-driven and not simply YoY-comparable: Q1 FY26 Rs293cr -> Q1 FY27 Rs107cr (down sharply on delivery timing) even as presales/collections grew. FY-level revenue: FY23 Rs410cr -> FY24 Rs944cr (+130%) -> FY25 Rs529cr (-44%, low-completion year) -> FY26 Rs1,143cr (+116%, record). Bookings/presales (the real demand signal) grew every year: FY24 Rs1,798cr -> FY25 Rs1,937cr (+7.7%) -> FY26 ~+25% YoY per company release.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~32.5x trailing P/E is rich for a lumpy-earnings developer; the market is paying more for the senior-living growth optionality (bookings/collections trajectory) than for the reported P&L trend, which does not move cleanly year to year.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Senior-living capex funded largely from internal accruals/collections (D/E just 0.30, net debt ~Rs958cr, Debt/CFO ~0.5x per ICRA); strategic land acquisitions in Pune, Chennai (MWC lease) and Maharashtra funded without large incremental borrowing; no unrelated diversification found in sources reviewed
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit mix-shift up the value chain from plain residential to higher-realization, stickier senior-living format (41% of Q1 FY27 bookings vs ~25%+ a year prior, target ~50%), with recurring lifestyle-services revenue (dining, ~300 activities/month) layered on the one-time sale.

four_box.note: Senior-living demographics is a genuine structural multi-decade driver (India TAM ~USD3.55bn 2025 -> ~USD14.14bn 2031, Mordor Intelligence), confirmed by real FY26 bookings/collections growth, not just narrative. TAM headroom real: ~Rs8,000cr senior-living GDV pipeline of ~Rs16,000cr total vs Rs1,143cr FY26 base. Moat weak -- premium pricing (Rs15,200/sqft) and lifestyle differentiation are real but not structural; PE-backed entrants (Antara, Columbia Pacific, Primus) could erode the edge. Valuation weak -- ~32.5x trailing P/E / ~4.4x P/B already price in meaningful growth.

track_record.note: FY23-25 3-yr avg ROCE ~6.2% (median 3.7%, screener.in) never reached the 15% hurdle despite strong revenue growth in FY23/FY24; FY25 also failed the revenue-growth leg outright (-44%). FY26's 14.0% ROCE (on +116% revenue growth) is the closest miss -- just under the 15% bar -- a real but still-unconfirmed single-year inflection. Real-estate completion accounting makes per-year ROCE a volatile, imperfect read for this business model.

shareholding_pattern.note: Promoter holding flat at 61.11% Dec-2025 through Mar-2026 (effectively through Jun-2026 too); zero pledge across all four named promoter individuals (Varun/Ankur/Vishal/Rachna Gupta) throughout. FII+DII combined ~16.3% as of Jun-2026 (FII 8.2%, DII 8.1%) -- directional trend not independently confirmed this pass.
